author: DPA
title: US plans additional $242 million in Ebola aid for Africa - NewsBreak
text:
1 hours ago
FILE PHOTO - An Ebola nurse at the CTE ALIMA BENI Ebola Treatment Centre cares for a child suspected of having Ebola. (is associated with: «US plans additional $242 million in Ebola aid for Africa») Kitsa Musayi/dpa The administration of US President Donald Trump plans to provide an additional $242 million to help combat the Ebola outbreak in Africa, the State Department said on Wednesday.
The funding, which is subject to consultations with Congress, would support emergency response efforts, regional preparedness and humanitarian assistance related to the outbreak, the department said.
The announcement comes as the administration has scaled back international aid programmes since Trump took office in January 2025. It has cut foreign assistance, reviewed a range of international programmes and withdrawn the United States from the World Health Organization (WHO).
The State Department said the latest funding builds on US commitments made at the Group of Seven summit in June and would bring total direct US assistance to fight the Ebola outbreak to more than $512 million.
In addition, the administration said it would provide $350 million in humanitarian assistance for the Democratic Republic of Congo, South Sudan and Uganda. The funding is part of a previously announced $1.8 billion package for the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs and is intended to benefit several countries.
Ebola is a highly infectious and often fatal viral disease spread through direct contact with infected people or their bodily fluids.
Aid group Médecins Sans Frontières has described the outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as more critical than ever around two and a half months after it began. It is the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the country, with more than 3,600 laboratory-confirmed infections and about 1,500 deaths.
